patient.referral_reason: Right leg cellulitis / right leg pain; recently homeless
patient.care_setting: emergency department, no inpatient admission – applied as ED (CalAIM form 'Currently in Hospital? Yes' read as in the ED at referral)

patient_summary: 73-year-old woman (adult criteria) referred from the emergency department; she was not admitted (face sheet: Patient Class Emergency, inpatient admit N/A). EMS brought her from a grocery store parking lot. She reports being homeless for about 5 days, has no emergency contact, and has Medicare plus CalOptima Medi-Cal. Referral reason: right leg cellulitis, shin to toes. She was on oral doxycycline for 8 days and has felt 'sicker' for 2 days; in the ED she got IV cefepime, vancomycin and an LR bolus. Afebrile (36.6 C), HR 72, RR 16, SpO2 98% on room air, BP 178/79 on losartan. WBC 7.46, lactate 0.8, procalcitonin 0.10 (flagged), flu/RSV/COVID NAAT negative (date redacted), CXR without acute findings. PMH: paroxysmal AF s/p ablation, asthma, OSA on CPAP, bipolar 1, schizophrenia, GERD/Barrett, anemia, back injury. AOx4. Forms report independent ADLs, 100 ft with a seated walker and self-administered meds. Missing or open: blood/urine culture results, right foot X-ray and LE venous duplex (pending), 5 sets of vitals, a confirmed ECG read, PT/OT and psych notes marked as attached, and a discharge/antibiotic/home-health plan (MDM, impression and disposition are unfilled templates). Contradictions: apixaban status, walking ability, and IV antibiotics (form 'No' vs given in ED). No psychiatric medications are listed.

Confirm she is being discharged directly from the ED; if she is admitted, add a negative MRSA swab and a COVID swab within 24 hours of arrival.

On re-review, deny-level risks to check first: foot X-ray for osteomyelitis, culture results / vitals for sepsis, SI and command hallucinations, conservatorship/FSP history, and whether IV antibiotics continue without home health.
